message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001784","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (abdominal aortic aneurysm). Per the performance-metrics guidance (prs_model_evaluator skill section: performance_metrics), the most comparable cross-model signal is an explicit PRS-only / covariates-regressed-out metric rather than a full-model AUROC/C-index that can be heavily driven by age/sex and other covariates. Among the candidates, PGS001784 reports a PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out) of 0.014661 in a large European validation (n=350,767) and uses a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS-auto, 911,440 variants). Competing models either lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS000753, PGS003972/PGS003973), report only partial-r of similar magnitude but with smaller validation (PGS002054 partial-r=0.0144; n=19,545), or report only full-model metrics with unknown covariates (PGS003429). Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records for related ‘aortic aneurysm and dissection’ phenotypes show low observed-scale h2 but higher liability-scale h2 (~0.02 to ~0.106), so a PRS-only R2 around ~0.015 is plausible and not obviously inconsistent with a heritability ceiling; this supports treating PGS001784’s PRS-comparable R2 as credible evidence rather than relying on covariate-inflated full-model discrimination."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: the target is alcohol dependence; among candidates, PGS002738 and PGS002739 are labeled directly as alcohol use disorder / alcohol dependence (trait_efo=alcohol dependence), whereas PGS000201/PGS000202 are for “problematic alcohol use” with a DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype (more measurement/proxy-like). Ancestry/transport: PGS002738 is evaluated in EUR (100%), matching the common use context implied by the other EUR-evaluated candidates; PGS002739 is evaluated in AFR only, making it less directly applicable if EUR is desired. Performance evidence: while AUC/R2 are not reported, PGS002738 provides a clear case-control style discrimination metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, CI 1.54–2.51) with multiple performance records (record_count=4), suggesting more robustness than the single-record ΔR2-only reports for PGS000201/PGS000202. Validation size is also strong (n=7,900) and comparable to the best of the others. Method/variants: PRS-CS is a standard genome-wide approach; variant count (326k) is plausible and not so small as to suggest an overly constrained model. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records for alcohol dependence/alcohol-related traits are modest (e.g., h2~0.098 observed; liability h2~0.182 for an alcohol dependency discovery record), consistent with expecting only moderate PRS effect sizes—so the observed OR enrichment for the top decile is plausible rather than suspiciously inflated."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004913","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates match the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), so selection hinges on PRS-quality evidence and comparability. Per the performance-metrics guidance, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R²) are preferred over full-model discrimination; full-model AUC/C-index can be covariate-driven and is not the primary cross-model ranking axis. Among the candidates, PGS004913 reports an explicit variance explained (R²=0.029) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a direct endpoint (“Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis”), making its performance evidence more directly interpretable as PRS signal than PGS000704 (only full-model C-index 0.711 in a time-to-event model) and PGS001777 (only full-model AUROC 0.671 with unknown covariates, very small 3-variant score). As a sanity check, local EUR heritability records for related liver disease/cirrhosis endpoints show low observed-scale h² but non-trivial liability-scale h² (e.g., ICD10 K70 alcoholic liver disease h²_liability ~0.074; ICD10 K74 fibrosis/cirrhosis h²_liability ~0.92), so an R² of 0.029 is plausible and not suggestive of metric misuse. Overall, PGS004913 offers the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence with good endpoint fidelity, hence the best choice, with moderate confidence due to limited cross-ancestry validation and modest training/validation sizes."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Selected PGS001262 because it is a direct endpoint match to angina pectoris with explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.01304) and basic covariate adjustment (age, sex, array, PCs), which is the most reliable basis for cross-model comparison per the performance-metrics guidance (PRS-only metrics > full-model AUROC). Among candidates with PRS-only metrics (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262), PGS001262 has the strongest PRS-only AUROC/R2 and the largest incremental AUROC (0.0098), while alternatives either lack PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS000703 full-model AUROC only; PGS004457/PGS004527 OR only; MVP-based 2024 scores report full-model C-index without PRS-only separation) or use a time-to-event phenotype (PGS001261) that is less directly comparable to a cross-sectional angina diagnosis. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR LDSC records for ICD10 I20 Angina pectoris show observed h2 ~0.012–0.016 (liability h2 ~0.09–0.19), consistent with the modest PRS-only R2 (~0.013) reported for PGS001262, supporting that the PRS-only metric is in a plausible range rather than being dominated by covariate packaging."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001268","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates target ankylosing spondylitis, but PGS001268 is the strongest direct-endpoint option with clearly reported PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.7346; PGS-only R²=0.1023) and a slightly better selected European validation full-model AUROC (0.7488) than its closest sibling PGS001267. The alternative UKB portability-study scores (PGS001876/PGS002089) report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), making them less directly comparable for discrimination; the Taiwan EAS-only models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation N (n=1,298), so their higher AUROC is not reliable evidence of stronger standalone PRS performance. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR LDSC records for ankylosing spondylitis show liability-scale h2 in the ~0.14–0.40 range (e.g., ICD10 M45 h2_liability≈0.399), so a PRS-only R² around 0.10 is plausible and not obviously inflated, supporting PGS001268 as a high-quality direct choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait match: PGS005252 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly match aortic stenosis (incident aortic stenosis cases). Other candidates are hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or aortic valve function measurements, so they are less endpoint-faithful for the target.

Evidence-weighting per skill guidance (performance_metrics section): the reported C-index=0.87 is a full-model metric and includes multiple clinical covariates (age/sex/PCs plus cardiometabolic comorbidities), so it should not be interpreted as PRS-only discrimination. However, among the direct aortic stenosis scores, PGS005252 provides the strongest overall package: modern genome-wide method (LDPred2), very large variant count (~1.12M), and large European evaluation sample (n=446,895), with an HR=1.92 supporting meaningful risk stratification.

Comparison to other aortic stenosis candidates: PGS005254 reports only HR=1.64 with no AUC/C-index and smaller evaluation N (n=244,450); PGS005255/PGS005256 are primarily valve-function measurement scores (not the disease endpoint) and have weaker HR (~1.53).

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records): the local h2 lookup for the string "aortic stenosis" returned only non-matching "stenosis" traits (match_score 0.0 across records), so there is no reliable trait-specific h2 ceiling available here to further contextualize PRS R²/AUC. This increases uncertainty, but does not outweigh the direct endpoint match and stronger study/score characteristics of PGS005252 within the fixed candidate set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is broad “arthritis”; among candidates, PGS001135 is the only model whose trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “arthritis” / “Arthritis (nos)”, giving the best endpoint fidelity per the trait-label guidance (phenotyping_reported is the primary alignment field). Its evaluation is European with a large validation sample (n=24,905) and it reports both PRS-only and full-model metrics, reducing ambiguity about covariate-driven performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.539; incremental AUROC 0.00314). Although several subtype arthritis scores show higher full-model AUROC (e.g., spondyloarthropathy, juvenile idiopathic arthritis subtypes), those are endpoint-mismatched to generic arthritis and often have small validation Ns or unclear covariate packaging. Heritability look-up for “arthritis” shows low-to-modest SNP h2 for broad/unspecified arthritis phenotypes (e.g., UKBB self-reported arthritis (nos) h2 ~0.0006–0.0045; ICD10 M13 other arthritis h2 ~0.0024–0.0073), consistent with the modest PRS-only performance observed for PGS001135 and supporting it as a plausible best available direct-match score in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Chose PGS001344 (Asthma diagnosed by doctor; snpnet) because it has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence among direct asthma endpoints: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.64568; PGS R2 no covariates 0.05973) and a clean, basic covariate set (age, sex, array, PCs), which the performance-metrics guidance treats as the most reliable basis for cross-model comparison. Competing candidates often report only full-model AUROC (potentially covariate-inflated), only incremental R2, or non-comparable endpoints (e.g., pediatric/childhood asthma, time-to-event, algorithmic definitions) despite sometimes larger N. The asthma heritability lookup shows EUR SNP-heritability estimates typically around ~0.05–0.19 depending on definition/source (e.g., UKBB doctor-diagnosed asthma h2 ~0.05; GWAS Atlas asthma h2 up to ~0.19), making the observed PGS-only R2 (~0.06) plausible and supportive rather than suspicious. Overall, PGS001344 offers the best combination of endpoint fidelity, PRS-only metric availability, and strong discrimination within this candidate set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is atopic eczema. Endpoint fidelity: PGS002755 has trait_efo=atopic eczema and phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis in a very large European validation sample (n=337,910), which is a strong direct-match disease endpoint compared with several candidates that are therapy-specific/paradoxical eczema in psoriasis patients (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903) and thus endpoint-mismatched for generic atopic eczema risk (per trait-label guidance that treatment-induced/therapy-specific endpoints are warning signals). PGS001773 is also aligned to atopic eczema but is restricted to moderate-to-severe disease and reports only full-model performance (AUROC 0.93) with multiple covariates, making the PRS contribution hard to compare and with much smaller validation (n=676). PGS004587 is incident AD but uses only 23 genome-wide significant SNPs and reports a modest HR (1.153), whereas PGS002755 uses a modern genome-wide PRS-CS model with ~1.09M variants and shows a clearer risk gradient (HR 1.249, high vs low PRS) in the same large-scale incident setting. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 for eczema is modest (h2~0.071; liability h2~0.129), so extremely high full-model AUROC values are plausibly driven by covariates/packaging rather than pure PRS signal; this supports preferring the large-scale, genome-wide PRS with direct incident endpoint over small-N, covariate-heavy full-model metrics. Overall, PGS002755 is the best direct-match candidate available, though sub-optimal because it lacks directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R2 in the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000327 is the most endpoint-faithful candidate: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to autism spectrum disorder, whereas PGS002790 has a mismatched phenotyping_reported field (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”), which is a material endpoint-fidelity concern per the evaluation framework (read_skill_section: skill_overview). On the comparable performance evidence available, PGS000327 also shows stronger reported predictive signal (full-model R²=0.0245; OR=1.33) than PGS002790 (partial R²≈0.0055), with a larger validation sample (7,148 vs 2,198) and clearly described ASD-focused training cohorts. Heritability lookups for autism spectrum disorder in EUR show non-trivial SNP-heritability in some records (e.g., h2≈0.19–0.29 from gwas_atlas), making an R² on the order of a few percent plausible and supporting that PGS000327’s reported performance is within a reasonable range for the trait (get_heritability_records: autism spectrum disorder)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000448","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma) and are evaluated in Europeans with broadly comparable basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch) for the PRSweb-derived set. Per the performance-metrics guidance (prs_model_evaluator skill section: performance_metrics), none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2, so full-model AUROC differences are not a reliable cross-model discriminator; instead, effect-size magnitude and other supportive signals are used. Within the PRSweb 2020-12-15 family, PGS000448 (lassosum, 183 variants) shows the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.411, 95% CI 1.335–1.491) and the strongest top-1% vs rest enrichment (OR 2.93, 95% CI 2.03–4.25), with a competitive full-model AUROC (0.587) under basic covariates—making it the best-supported choice among the fixed candidates. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR LDSC records for self-reported basal cell carcinoma show low observed-scale h2 (~0.01–0.013) but substantially higher liability-scale h2 (~0.14–0.21), consistent with modest-to-moderate PRS discrimination and supporting that the observed effect sizes are plausible rather than implausibly high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000924","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000924 is the strongest direct match to the target trait within the fixed list: it explicitly targets disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event) and includes bilirubin metabolism disease in trait_efo. It also provides clear, comparable discrimination/variance metrics with both PGS-only and full-model results (PGS-only AUROC 0.88697; PGS-only R² 0.21843; full-model AUROC 0.90591), whereas PGS001824 and PGS002032 report only partial correlation (partial-r 0.0716) without AUROC/R², making head-to-head performance comparison weaker. Although PGS000924 uses very few variants (5), its reported predictive performance is substantially stronger than the portability-study scores in this candidate set, and it has a large UKB training sample (n=269,704) with European validation (n=67,425). Trait heritability lookups for closely related bilirubin measures in EUR show modest h2 (e.g., ~0.089 and lower in the returned records), which supports interpreting very high full-model metrics cautiously; however, PGS000924’s strong PGS-only metrics still make it the best-supported choice among the available candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Target trait is bipolar disorder. Among candidates, PGS002786 is the only one whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly match bipolar disorder (the others are bipolar I and bipolar II subtypes). However, endpoint fidelity is weak across this whole set: phenotyping_reported fields are not direct bipolar disorder diagnosis endpoints (they are cognition/behavior measures), which the trait-label guidance flags as a warning signal for deployment to a generic disease target (read_skill_section('trait_labels')). Reported performance is also only a small partial R² (~0.0025) in a modest European validation sample (n=2,524), so overall quality is limited. Heritability lookups for bipolar disorder in EUR show substantial SNP h2 on the liability scale in some GWAS-Atlas records (~0.17–0.27), indicating the trait is meaningfully heritable, but these candidates’ reported partial R² is far below that ceiling and likely reflects the non-diagnostic evaluation phenotype rather than strong disease prediction (get_heritability_records('bipolar disorder')). Given the fixed list, PGS002786 is the closest direct match by trait label, but the recommendation is sub-optimal due to phenotype mismatch and weak reported predictive signal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait alignment: PGS001033 has trait_efo exactly matching the target (blood coagulation disease) and a closely aligned endpoint (“Other coagulation defects (time-to-event)”), whereas PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the same EFO as the target). Performance evidence: PGS001033 provides directly comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.634; full-model AUROC 0.656 with standard covariates), while the other two candidates report only partial correlation (partial-r ~0.056) without AUROC/R², making cross-candidate comparison less direct. Study/validation context: PGS001033 is trained in UKB (n≈269k) and has a larger reported validation sample size (n≈67k) with explicit covariates listed, supporting interpretability of the reported metrics. Heritability sanity-check: a lookup for “blood coagulation disease” returned no matching h2 records, so no h2-based calibration of the observed performance is possible; the choice therefore rests primarily on endpoint fidelity and the availability/clarity of performance metrics per the evaluation framework in the PRS model evaluator skill overview."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is breast carcinoma; several candidates directly match via trait_efo=\"breast carcinoma\". Per the PRS evaluator guidance, prioritize endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence over covariate-boosted full-model AUC alone (read_skill_section: skill_overview, performance_metrics). Among direct-match models, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) reports strong PRS-only/PRS-comparable evidence with covariates explicitly set to 0, including AUROC 0.6625 and R² 0.0764 in European validation (n=48,968), indicating substantial standalone genetic discrimination without clinical-risk-factor packaging. Competing direct-match options often report only full-model AUC with nontrivial clinical covariates (e.g., age/family history/lifestyle) or lack PRS-only metrics, making cross-model comparison less reliable. Heritability sanity check: local EUR h2 lookups for the exact string \"breast carcinoma\" return mostly weak/poorly matched carcinoma-in-situ ICD10 records (match_score 0.0) with low observed h2, so they are not very informative for setting a ceiling here; nonetheless, PGS004153’s PRS R² is not implausibly extreme and is supported by clean (covariate-free) reporting (get_heritability_records: breast carcinoma)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001301","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait alignment: PGS001301 targets “Malabsorption/coeliac disease” with trait_efo exactly “celiac disease”, which is acceptably close to the requested celiac disease endpoint, whereas some alternatives are explicitly restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (PGS000041/PGS000042) or broaden to gluten sensitivity (PGS001894/PGS002107). Performance evidence quality: PGS001301 is the only candidate providing clearly comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.8287; PGS-only R² 0.1422) alongside a covariate-adjusted full-model AUROC (0.8335), reducing ambiguity about covariate “packaging” versus standalone PRS signal per the evaluation guidance (skill_overview). Other candidates either report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (e.g., PGS000040 AUROC 0.90; PGS000316 AUROC 0.879) or provide partial correlation rather than AUROC/R² (PGS001856/PGS002067), making cross-candidate comparison less clean. Scale/robustness: PGS001301 is trained in a large UKB sample (n=269,704) with a substantial European validation set (n=67,425). Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records for celiac disease show non-trivial liability-scale heritability (e.g., h2_liability ~0.15–0.45 across sources), consistent with a PRS explaining a meaningful fraction of variance; PGS001301’s PRS-only R² (~0.14) is plausible in that context and supports it as the best-supported, directly relevant choice among the fixed candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001174","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS001174 is the strongest direct-match candidate for cholelithiasis with the cleanest, most comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.623 and PGS R2(no covariates)=0.028) plus full-model and incremental AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), aligning with the performance-metrics guidance that PRS-only metrics are the most reliable cross-model comparator (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview; performance_metrics). Competing direct-endpoint models (PGS004476/PGS004546) provide only per-SD ORs (~1.22–1.30, i.e., modest) and have unknown covariates, reducing comparability; the portability-study scores (PGS001861/PGS002072) target a broader phenotype (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and report only partial-r, not PRS-only AUROC/R2. Heritability records for ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis in EUR show observed h2 ~0.013–0.029 (liability h2 ~0.12–0.15), making PGS001174’s PRS-only R2=0.028 a plausible magnitude (not exceeding a reasonable genetic-variance ceiling) and supporting that its reported PRS signal is credible rather than obviously inflated (get_heritability_records: cholelithiasis)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity is strongest for PGS002237: it is explicitly chronic kidney disease stage ≥3 with a clear eGFR threshold (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), matching the target trait (CKD) more directly than candidates that are time-to-event chronic renal failure (PGS001272), CKD bundled with dialysis (PGS003988+ family), or CKD defined in special contexts (e.g., secondhand smoke exposure PGS004224; incident CKD without diabetes PGS004889). Per the performance-metrics guidance (read_skill_section: performance_metrics), full-model AUROC should not be treated as PRS-only; however, among the candidates, PGS002237 comes from a disease-focused Nat Med study designed to predict CKD across ancestries with broad evaluation ancestries, and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.47) alongside a high full-model AUROC (0.78). Competing models either lack comparable PRS-only metrics and/or show weaker PRS-only discrimination where available (e.g., PGS001272 has PGS-only AUROC ~0.536 and PGS-only R2 ~0.002). The CKD heritability lookup (get_heritability_records) shows EUR observed h2 estimates around ~0.012–0.019 (liability ~0.039–0.057), which supports interpreting modest PRS-only R2 values as plausible and cautions against over-weighting covariate-heavy full-model AUROCs; nonetheless, given the combination of direct CKD endpoint definition, multi-ancestry evaluation context, and moderate-to-strong effect size evidence, PGS002237 is the best overall candidate in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS001783 is a direct match to the target trait (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; trait_efo matches). Several alternatives are COPD subtypes/definitions (algorithmic, time-to-event, ICD10 J44) or a related but not identical endpoint (emphysema; chronic airway obstruction).

Performance interpretation (per prs_model_evaluator performance_metrics guidance): prioritize PRS-comparable metrics over full-model AUROC. PGS001783 reports a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 of 0.0381, which is substantially higher than the UKB snpnet COPD scores’ PGS-only R2 (~0.00235–0.00314) and provides clearer evidence of standalone PRS signal than candidates that only report partial-r or per-SD OR without discrimination metrics.

Study/context signals: PGS001783 comes from a multi-biobank PRS-CS-auto framework (Cell Genomics) with multi-ancestry GWAS inputs and European evaluation, which is generally a stronger PRS construction approach than sparse UKB-only snpnet models when the reported PRS-comparable R2 is also higher.

Heritability sanity check: local EUR h2 records for COPD-related endpoints (e.g., UKB ICD10 J44 and doctor-diagnosed COPD) show observed-scale h2 on the order of ~0.003–0.025 (with liability-scale values higher). A PRS-comparable R2 of 0.038 is plausible given scale differences (Nagelkerke/covariates-regressed-out vs observed h2) and does not appear obviously inconsistent; it supports that PGS001783 is capturing meaningful genetic signal relative to the other candidates’ much smaller PRS-only R2."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is cirrhosis of liver; the most endpoint-faithful candidates are those with trait_efo = \"cirrhosis of liver\" (PGS000726, PGS000776, PGS004621). Among these, PGS004621 is the strongest overall-quality record on visible metadata: it uses a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS) with very broad variant coverage (1,089,806 variants) and is evaluated in a very large European validation sample (n=1,153,995) with standard covariates (age, sex, 10 PCs) and AUROC reported (0.68). Competing direct-EFO options either lack standard discrimination metrics entirely (PGS000726 reports ORs but no AUC/R2) or are more narrowly alcohol-related / smaller-training-context (PGS000776 has C-index 0.677 and a less direct phenotyping description). Heritability context for cirrhosis-related UKB endpoints is low on the observed scale (e.g., h2 ~0.0007–0.0083 from local LDSC records), so modest AUROC values are plausible and do not contradict the choice; given similar performance magnitudes across candidates, the much larger validation and genome-wide construction of PGS004621 make it the best-supported direct cirrhosis PGS here."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are a direct endpoint match (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported) from the same UKB portability paper, with the same training N (391,124), validation ancestry (European selected), validation N (19,864), and the same basic covariate set. The only differentiators are method/architecture and variant count, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2—only a very similar partial correlation (0.0562 vs 0.0563), which is effectively a tie per the performance-metrics guidance (PRS-comparable metrics are preferred; small gaps are not meaningful). In this tie, prefer the more expressive genome-wide LDpred2 model with many variants (32,552) over a sparse penalized-regression model with 45 variants, as a stronger structural signal for capturing polygenic signal. Heritability lookup for the target string did not return a clear matching record for this rare coagulation-factor deficiency (returned unrelated vitamin traits with match_score 0), so h2 cannot further calibrate expectations here; this lowers confidence but does not change the within-list choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Corneal dystrophy”) and come from the same UKB portability study with the same training N (391,124), validation ancestry context, validation N (19,321 Europeans), and similar basic covariate adjustment (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, PCs). With endpoint and study context essentially tied, the most comparable differentiator is the PRS-comparable performance signal available here: the selected European validation record reports a higher partial correlation for PGS002042 (partial-r=0.0471, CI 0.033–0.0611) than PGS001835 (partial-r=0.0384, CI 0.0243–0.0525), supporting slightly stronger standalone genetic signal. This also aligns with structural expectations from the performance-metrics guidance: when PRS-only AUC/R2 are missing, modest PRS-comparable metrics plus stronger model structure/coverage can break ties; PGS002042 uses LDpred2 with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is a supportive robustness signal within the same publication family. Heritability sanity-check was attempted via get_heritability_records for “corneal dystrophy” but returned no matching records, so no h2-based calibration is possible; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Selected PGS000013 (LDpred; 6.6M variants) because it is a direct endpoint match to coronary artery disease and, per the performance-metrics guidance, it is one of the few candidates reporting an explicit PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke/PGS-only R2=0.04) rather than only covariate-inflated full-model discrimination. Its validation sample size is large (n=288,978, European), and covariates are relatively standard (age, sex, PCs, chip), making the reported PRS contribution more interpretable than candidates with only full-model AUC/C-index or unknown/heavy clinical covariates. Heritability lookups for coronary artery disease in EUR show observed h2 around ~0.065–0.096 (with liability-scale estimates ~0.06–0.12), so an R2 of 0.04 is plausible and not suspiciously above the trait’s genetic-variance ceiling, supporting that the metric is on a reasonable scale.
